GOAL: Map both finalist mechanisms onto rubric-2026-10-v1 and test each against the shared frozen evidence bundle.
READ: Full idea text for A=SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ and B=cocond-markov-poincare-ot, plus both bundles (A: 404ea254563870a6, B: bc19762831440f87) and the third-family bundle CURVCELL-SID (e9e97242e0e9ed08) as prior art.
OBSERVED:
- The two bundles are near-identical on the OBSERVED block: E5 (successor-entropy quintiles: bin1 distinct 2.72 top1 0.4375; bin5 distinct 41.41 support 44.3 top1 0.0543; Spearman -0.9733), E6 (width-20 beam survival, best recall 0.06363 resample; l1_br 0.04671 with depth-4 prefix survival 0.068; l1_br_euclid depth1/2 = 1.000/0.829), E7 (teacher-forced NLL; baseline reported_test_recall@10 0.04069), E8 (first-level capacity ceiling: share of canonical pairs sharing a K-cluster 0.3106 at K=16 falling monotonically to 0.0822 at K=256), E9 (positive shares successor cohort with anchor 0.9291 vs 0.8871 fixed negatives; profile overlap beats all ten negatives in 0.5898 of pairs), E10 (115,582 distinct edges, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, edge_density 5.3266), E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067).
- A's geometry appears only as a per-prefix scalar conformal factor lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) multiplying the residual at encode/decode; c_p in (0.1,10). Its matched Euclidean control (lambda=1) is literally plain RQ.
- B's geometry enters the Sinkhorn ground cost (Poincare distance via Mobius addition) and the codebook update (Klein/Einstein hyperbolic barycenter), i.e. it changes the argmax plan and the mean operator.
- CURVCELL-SID (third bundle) already derives per-codebook-entry curvature kappa[l][k] from a branching statistic B[l][k] and applies it inside the residual chain. A is the same branching->curvature->quantizer chain with the statistic moved from codebook entry to prefix node and the application moved from distance rescaling to residual rescaling.
REASONING: A scores well on implementability (scalar multiplies, <1% step cost, factorial USE_BEHAVIOUR x USE_HYPERBOLIC switches) but poorly on novelty (routine variation of CURVCELL-SID, and the branching family already produced the weakest measured recalls in E6) and weakly on geometry_necessity (a per-node radial scalar is reproducible by a matched per-node Euclidean gain). B scores better on novelty and geometry_necessity but worse on implementability (Sinkhorn sweeps, straight-through plan, code-collapse risk, alpha/q "measured never tuned" under-specified). E8 is the discriminator: it says finer first-level resolution monotonically destroys behavioural co-location, which is the direction A pushes hubs toward, while B's diffusion co-locates transition-connected items, the direction E9 endorses. Weighted tally approx A 3.0 vs B 3.5.
OPEN: final winner, the three decisive arguments with evidence ids, and B's failure risk.

FINAL ANSWER (complete, self-contained)
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ
ARGUMENT:
1) novelty + exploration_value. A is a routine variation of CURVCELL-SID (bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08, E12: kappa[l][k] derived from a branching statistic B[l][k] and injected inside the residual chain); A changes only the aggregation level (codebook entry -> prefix node) and the injection site (distance rescale -> residual scale). The same branching family has already been measured and lost here: E6 gives l1_br recall@10 0.04671 and successor_entropy 0.05122 against l1_only 0.06233 and resample 0.06363. B instead moves the assignment plan itself (entropic-OT plan diffused along training transition edges, then a hyperbolic barycenter codebook step), a locus that none of the cited rounds touched, so its negative would still be informative rather than a near-repeat.
2) geometry_necessity. A's curvature never does geometric work: lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) is a per-node radial scalar multiplying the RQ residual (E12/E13), so a matched per-node Euclidean radial gain reproduces it and the c->0 control is just plain RQ - the curved operation is separable from the behaviour signal. B's curvature is load-bearing in two places a matched Euclidean control cannot copy: the Poincare ground cost inside the Sinkhorn kernel and the closed-form Klein/Einstein midpoint replacing the Euclidean code mean, so removing curvature changes the argmin plan and the codebook mean operator, not just a gain.
3) behavior_evidence against E8/E9. E8 measures that finer first-level resolution monotonically destroys behavioural co-location (share of canonical pairs sharing a K-cluster 0.3106 at K=16 -> 0.2164 at 32 -> 0.1547 at 64 -> 0.0822 at 256), which is exactly the direction A pushes the top-fanout quartile (E5: bin5 distinct successors 41.41 vs bin1 2.72). B pushes the other way, co-locating transition-connected items, which is what E9 supports (positive shares successor cohort with anchor 0.9291 vs 0.8871 for fixed negatives; 0.5898 of pairs beat all ten negatives) and what E6 shows separates winners from collapse (l1_br_euclid depth-2 prefix survival 0.829 vs l1_br 1.000 at depth 2 but 0.068 at depth 4, i.e. single-chain collapse).
FAILURE RISK: B's diffusion operator may be effectively the identity - E10 reports only 115,582 distinct edges at mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, so B_bt is sparse - in which case B degrades to plain curved-cost Sinkhorn, a family already at 0.05500 in E6, and the run fails for a reason unrelated to the assignment-plan idea; compounding this, B's success threshold of test Recall@10 > 0.065 sits above every measured value in E6 (max 0.06363) and E7 (baseline 0.04069), and the single-seed protocol cannot separate mechanism failure from seed noise, so an over-ambitious threshold could reject a mechanism that did move the assignment plan.

GOAL: head-to-head scoring of SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ (A) vs cocond-markov-poincare-ot (B) on rubric-2026-10-v1, same frozen bundles 404ea254563870a6 (A) and bc19762831440f87 (B), with the third bundled idea e9e97242e0e9ed08 (CURVCELL-SID) read only as prior-art context.
READ: A IDEA/SPEC (c_p in (0.1,10) per prefix node from popularity-adjusted fanout, lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2), gain at encode and inverse at decode, switches USE_BEHAVIOUR and USE_HYPERBOLIC); B SPEC steps 1-6 (exp_0, Mobius d_kappa, K=exp(-D/tau), 3 sweeps of P<-P/rowsum; P<-(1-alpha)P+alpha(B_bt@P); P<-P*q/colsum; j*(i)=argmax; EinsteinMidpoint codebook); E1-E13 of both bundles.
OBSERVED: (i) A's curved operation is a scalar gain on the residual: argmin_j||lambda*r - c_j||^2 = argmin_j(lambda*||r||^2 - 2 r.c_j + ||c_j||^2/lambda), a per-node codebook-radius rescale that a matched Euclidean per-prefix gain g_p built from the same fanout reproduces exactly -> geometry_necessity ~2 (A E12-E13). (ii) A's two ablations are degenerate: all c_p=1 gives a constant lambda, and the c->0 limit gives lambda=2 by the stated formula (not lambda=1 as A's SPEC asserts); a constant factor cancels between encode and decode, so both "controls" reduce to plain RQ -> falsifiability/implementability defect and an arithmetic inconsistency in the SPEC. (iii) A's curvature-from-branching is already CURVCELL-SID (kappa[l][k]=(log(1+B[l][k])/((d-1)R))^2 from per-cell successor branching, e9e97242e0e9ed08 E12); A changes only the aggregation unit and the injection -> novelty 1-2, and A's own novelty text concedes per-branch curvature existed. (iv) B's geometry sits inside the assignment (Poincare ground cost + Klein/Einstein barycentre, B E12-E13) with a real matched Euclidean control (Euclidean cost kernel + Euclidean mean, same diffusion) -> geometry 3. (v) B's new computation, one Markov step alpha*(B_bt@P) on the OT plan, is absent from the cited ledger (geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent successor residuals, per-branch curvature, geodesic prefix losses) and moves the plan, not a side loss -> novelty 4. (vi) Behaviour is a shared bundle: A's premise is strongly measured (E5 fanout bins 2.723->41.41 distinct successors, top1 0.4375->0.0543, Spearman -0.973, bin item counts = coverage) but A's own node-level statistic is unmeasured; B's problem is measured with a null (E11 same_first_prefix 0.0907 vs permuted 0.067; E10 mean out-degree 5.4526, 115582 distinct edges) though the margin is thin. (vii) Downstream: E6/E7 on 57439 test rows show all frozen SID variants plateau at recall@10 0.0467-0.0636 against the 0.065 gate, gold prefix alive at depth 4 only 0.068-0.086; E8 K=256 level-1 cluster sharing 0.0822 vs 0.0129 for negatives localises the ceiling in the level-1 assignment, which B changes and A cannot (A's root gain is near-global).
REASONING: A forfeits 40% of the weight (geometry 20 + novelty 20) to a matched scalar gain and to an idea already in the bundle; B wins downstream_mechanism (named j*(i) and barycentre weights, two named observables with expected directions, plus the discriminating diagnostic "a rises while c does not"), implementability (complete equations, straight-through gradient, norm clamp, named residual risks, ~5% overhead) and exploration_value (a plan-diffusion failure mode rather than another residual-space variant).
OPEN: B's dependence on a sparse B_bt and its collapse/single-seed risk; not decisive enough to change the ranking, recorded as the failure risk in the answer.

WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ
ARGUMENT: 1) geometry_necessity, and it is also a falsifiability defect: A's curved operation is a scalar gain on the residual, lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) applied at encode and divided at decode (A E12-E13); since argmin_j||lambda*r - c_j||^2 = argmin_j(lambda*||r||^2 - 2 r.c_j + ||c_j||^2/lambda), A is exactly a per-node codebook-radius rescale that a matched Euclidean per-prefix gain g_p built from the same fanout reproduces (rubric level 2). Both of A's ablations are degenerate in the same way: all c_p=1 gives a constant lambda, and the c->0 limit gives lambda=2 by the stated formula, not lambda=1 as the SPEC claims, and a constant factor cancels between encode and decode, so A's "three switches" are one condition; B's curvature is a Poincare distance and Klein/Einstein barycentre inside the assignment (B E12-E13) with a matched Euclidean-cost/Euclidean-mean control, so its switch switches something. 2) novelty: A's curvature is derived from successor branching, which is already CURVCELL-SID in this same bundle (kappa[l][k]=(log(1+B[l][k])/((d-1)R))^2 from per-cell successor branching, e9e97242e0e9ed08 E12); A changes only the aggregation unit (prefix node vs codebook entry) and the injection (conformal scalar vs rescaled distance), a routine variation/rename, and A's own novelty text concedes per-branch curvature was already tried, whereas B's Markov step alpha*(B_bt@P) on the entropic-OT plan (B SPEC steps 4-5) is absent from the cited ledger (geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent successor residuals, per-branch curvature, geodesic prefix losses) and moves the assignment plan itself. 3) downstream_mechanism and behaviour_evidence: E6/E7 on the 57439-row test split put every frozen SID variant at recall@10 0.0467-0.0636 against the 0.065 gate with the gold prefix alive at depth 4 in only 0.068-0.086 of rows, and E8's level-1 ceiling (K=256 anchor/target cluster sharing 0.0822 vs 0.0129 for negatives) puts the loss in the level-1 assignment, which B changes and A cannot (A's root gain is near-global); B names the affected assignment j*(i) and the barycentre weights, the two observables with expected directions, and a discriminating diagnostic ("a rises while c does not => decorative structure"), while A names only a residual gain and its stated success statistic (code entropy in the top fanout quartile) is not in the bundle, whereas B's premise is at least measured with a null (E11 same_first_prefix 0.0907 vs permuted 0.067; E10 mean out-degree 5.4526).
FAILURE RISK: B's required signal is thin - mean out-degree 5.4526 (E10) and 0.0907 vs a 0.067 permuted null for same-first-prefix (E11) imply B_bt is near-diagonal, so the alpha-diffusion may move almost no plan mass, and Sinkhorn plus a straight-through estimator plus a boundary-seeking hyperbolic barycentre can collapse codes and land the run at 0.05-0.06 recall, indistinguishable from seed noise in a single-seed protocol; the choice would also be wrong if a matched Euclidean per-prefix gain (A's real and far cheaper control) reproduces A's entropy/recall lift, or if the Poincare cost kernel turns out order-equivalent to Euclidean cost so that B's curvature is decorative too and every gain is attributable to the diffusion.

STAGE 1 - PLAN AND DIMENSION MAP
Goal: compare the two finalists (A=SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ, bundle 404ea254563870a6; B=cocond-markov-poincare-ot, bundle bc19762831440f87) on rubric-2026-10-v1, judging mechanisms only, not print order.
Read: the two idea texts (MOTIVATION/NOVELTY/CHANGE/SPEC/HYPOTHESIS/RISKS), both evidence bundles, and the third bundle (CURVCELL-SID, e9e97242e0e9ed08) because it is part of the same ledger and is needed to judge novelty.
Observed: the behavioural block E5-E11 is frozen and shared by all three bundles (identical strings), so E5-E11 cannot distinguish the candidates; only E12/E13 (geometric necessity) and the idea text differ. Both geometric-necessity blocks are truncated in the bundle (A's E14 is empty; B's E13 stops mid-sentence at "between the exp-mapped residual and the"), so geometric necessity must be judged from the SPEC equations, not from E12/E13 prose.
Key evidence I will lean on: E5 hub heterogeneity (top-1 mass 0.4375 -> 0.0543, H 0.931 -> 3.405), E6 beam survival + recall per variant (l1_br 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, resample 0.06363, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, _v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500), E8 first-level capacity ceiling (K=16 0.3106 -> K=256 0.0822, negatives 0.1352 -> 0.0129), E10 edge density 5.3266 / mean out-degree 5.4526 / 118315 edges, E11 same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067.
Reasoning so far: the discrimination will come from (a) whether the curved operation is scalar (A) or genuinely non-scalar (B); (b) whether A is a variation of the already-measured per-branch-curvature family (CURVCELL-SID plus the three negative geodesic variants in E6); (c) which mechanism actually touches the assignment, given E11's near-null prefix rate.
Open: confirm A's numeric domain for lambda_p and the encode/decode cancellation argument; confirm B's batch-sparsity dilution using E10 arithmetic; then score and pick.

STAGE 2 - THREE DECISIVE CHECKS (condensed)
(1) GEOMETRY (20%). A: lambda_p=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) is a positive scalar on the residual, multiplied at encode and divided at decode (A SPEC). argmin||lambda_p r - c|| = argmin||r - c/lambda_p||, a per-prefix Euclidean codebook gain; matched Euclidean control trivially constructible => rubric 2. The decode division cancels the encode amplification, so "more resolution" is notional and the real effect is a per-node scalar retune. Domain is invalid: c_p in (0.1,10) puts a pole at ||r||=1/sqrt(c_p) (0.316 for c_p=10) and lambda goes NEGATIVE beyond it, so a unit-norm RQ residual is sign-flipped; A's RISKS calls this "stiff" and no clamp is written. c_p map unspecified (E2 truncates at "For level-l"). A=2. B: Poincare cost 2*artanh(||(-p)(+)c||) is radially nonlinear and Klein Einstein-midpoint weights depend on norms, so no scalar/affine Euclidean control reproduces cost or mean; switches remove behaviour (plan + barycenter weights) and remove curvature (kernel + mean operator) inside one assignment block; cancellations not fully ruled out (ST desync) and E13 is truncated => 4.
(2) NOVELTY (20%) + EXPLORATION (5%). A is a variation of CURVCELL-SID (bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08, E12: kappa[l][k] from successor branching B[l][k]) and B's novelty text already lists "per-branch curvature" as done here; A's only delta is where the scalar is applied. E6 contains three measured negatives in that family: successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, _v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, all below l1_br_euclid 0.06207 (successor_entropy 0.05122 worse). A novelty 2, exploration 1-2. B moves the assignment plan, absent from the measured ledger; its null would be informative (is the transition graph too sparse to steer an assignment) => novelty 4, exploration 5.
(3) BEHAVIOUR (20%) + DOWNSTREAM (15%). E11 same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067: the prefix carries almost no successor structure, so the deficit is in the assignment, which is what B changes. E8 co-location falls monotonically 0.3106 (K=16) -> 0.0822 (K=256), negatives 0.1352 -> 0.0129: finer resolution pushes behavioural neighbours apart, the opposite of A's "more resolution for hubs" premise. E6: euclid keeps gold prefix at depth 2/3 = 0.829/0.161 at recall 0.06207 vs l1_br depth3 1.000 but depth4 0.068 at 0.04671. E5 (top-1 0.4375 vs 0.0543, H 0.931->3.405, 4895 items/bin) does show hubs are real, so A's premise is not fabricated but its remedy runs against E8. A behaviour 3, downstream 3 (assignment change unnamed, chain to recall unspecified). B behaviour 4, downstream 4 (names j*(i) and barycenter weights, observables a/b/c with directions and the discriminator "if (a) rises while (c) does not, decorative").
Rest: A falsifiability 3 (three switch cells incl. plain-RQ null, 0.065 bar, no refutation), implementability 3. B falsifiability 4, implementability 3 (alpha and q deferred to a missing SAFEGUARDS block; cost line wrong: 3x(BxB)@(BxK) at 1024x1024x256 ~5e8 MACs, not "5-8 MFLOPs", though at E10 in-batch density ~23% still only a few percent of a step).
Weighted: A = 60+40+40+45+30+30+5 = 2.50. B = 80+80+80+60+40+30+25 = 3.95. Winner B; A was printed first, order is not the reason.
Open: caveat for FAILURE RISK only (B's in-batch transition sparsity); carried into the final record.

STAGE 3 - FINAL VERDICT (complete answer)
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ
ARGUMENT: (1) geometry_necessity (20%): A's only curved object is the scalar conformal factor lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) written in its SPEC/E12, applied to the residual at encode and divided out at decode. Since argmin||lambda_p r - c|| = argmin||r - c/lambda_p||, a per-prefix Euclidean codebook gain reproduces it exactly, and the encode/decode division cancels the amplification, so the "more resolution" claim is a notional scalar retune; moreover with c_p in (0.1,10) lambda has a pole at ||r||=1/sqrt(c_p) and turns negative beyond it, so the operation is not even a valid metric on unit-norm residuals (A's RISKS calls it merely "stiff"). That is rubric 2. B's cost is the radially nonlinear 2*artanh(||(-p)(+)c||) with a Klein Einstein midpoint whose weights depend on the point norms (E12/E13), which no scalar or affine Euclidean control reproduces, and its two switches change the plan plus the barycenter weights and the cost kernel plus the mean operator inside one assignment block (rubric 4).
(2) novelty (20%) plus exploration_value (5%): A is a variation of CURVCELL-SID, which already derives a per-codebook-entry curvature kappa[l][k] from successor branching B[l][k] (bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08, E12), and the ledger already contains per-branch curvature; A's only delta is where the same scalar is applied. Its family has three measured negatives in E6 - successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500 - all below l1_br_euclid 0.06207 (successor_entropy 0.05122 is worse), so it is a small variation of a measured mechanism inside a family that already lost. B moves the assignment plan itself, which no listed mechanism does, and its negative would answer a live question (whether this transition graph is dense enough to steer an assignment).
(3) behaviour_evidence (20%) plus downstream_mechanism (15%): E11 gives same-first-prefix 0.0907 against a permuted null of 0.067, i.e. the SID prefix carries almost no successor structure, so the deficit is in the assignment - exactly what B rewrites and what A leaves untouched. E8 shows behavioural co-location falling monotonically from 0.3106 at K=16 to 0.0822 at K=256 (negatives 0.1352 to 0.0129), so making hub prefixes finer runs against the measured gradient of A's own remedy, while E6 shows the cost of the other direction (l1_br keeps the gold prefix to depth 3 at 1.000 but only 0.068 at depth 4, recall 0.04671 vs 0.06207 for the euclid control). E5 (top-1 mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543, H 0.931 to 3.405, 4895 items per bin) does establish that hubs exist, so A's premise is not fabricated, but its chain names no assignment change and no direction to recall, whereas B names the plan j*(i), the barycenter weights, the three observables with expected directions, and the discriminator "if (a) rises while (c) does not, the coupling is decorative".
FAILURE RISK: B's behaviour channel can be diluted to near-identity: with 118315 edges over 24556 items and mean out-degree 5.4526 (E10), the chance that an item's successor is in the same 1024-item batch is only about 0.23, so one Markov step leaves most plan rows unchanged after column renormalisation and the run silently degrades to plain curved Sinkhorn; if that alone does not clear l1_br_euclid 0.06207, B lands at baseline, and with a 0.065 bar only 0.0014 above the best measured probe (resample 0.06363) and a single seed, I could not separate mechanism failure from noise - which would hand the decision back to A's cheaper and cleanly ablated scalar.
